speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following your recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis. To evaluate this properly, have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as urgency, frequency, or the presence of blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of fatigue, fever, and flank pain persisting after treatment for sinusitis raise concern for an ascending infection. Do you experience burning sensations when urinating, or have you noticed cloudy or foul-smelling urine?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyelonephritis secondary to resistant E. coli infection, likely triggered by incomplete eradication of the initial sinusitis pathogen and potentially exacerbated by allergic reactions to beta-lactams (amoxicillin/cephalexin). The clinical triad of fever, flank pain, and fatigue post-antibiotic therapy for a urinary tract source (sinusitis can sometimes mask or coexist with UTIs, or the patient may have misidentified symptoms) strongly supports this. Immediate urine culture and renal imaging are required to confirm and rule out abscess formation.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, CBC
REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound
